attributions.claim: Fairbank described the radiographic changes that follow meniscectomy from clinical series in the middle of the twentieth century, before any mechanical explanation existed.
further_claims: Read Fairbank's observation and the modern trials together, because the second is the first with a control group.

attributions.claim: Walker and Erkman measured load transmission through the tibiofemoral joint with and without the menisci in the 1970s, using cadaveric specimens and pressure sensitive methods.
Seedhom worked on meniscal load bearing in the same period, separating the proportion of load the menisci carry from the proportion the exposed cartilage carries.
Fukubayashi and Kurosawa quantified contact area and contact pressure in the 1980s, with the menisci intact and after removal, at a range of flexion angles.
Shrive and colleagues examined the circumferential fibre architecture and showed how hoop tension converts a compressive load into a circumferential one.
Arnoczky and Warren mapped the meniscal blood supply, which set the boundary between the repairable periphery and the avascular inner zone.
